answer: An agent economy can require every new identity to stake scarce tokens and complete a useful task before it earns access to high-value contracts. Reputation grows only when independent counterparties verify delivered work, while fraud slashes the stake and resets that record. A sybil attacker must therefore lock up capital across many identities and pay the real cost of producing verifiable work; cheap names alone cannot climb from nadir to knoll or form an island of trusted accounts.
